title: Cycle Simulation: probabilistic burn curves, tranche reserve policy, and emergency trim playbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Context: As Redwood scales product delivery across multiple teams, we need a repeatable way to (1) forecast cycle burn under uncertain skill availability, (2) allocate a tranche reserve that balances delivery confidence with utilization, and (3) define a fast emergency trim protocol that preserves critical customer-facing deliverables. This ticket creates a practical playbook and a lightweight simulator to inform sprint commitments and mid-cycle decommits.

Goals:
- Ship a Monte Carlo style cycle simulator for senior PMs and IC leads that models probabilistic individual velocity, cross-team dependencies, and tranche reserves.
- Define tranche reserve policies (size, refresh cadence, activation criteria) and tie them to cycle-level SLOs and OKR risk thresholds.
- Produce an emergency trim runbook with roles, decision gates, and templated communications for scope cuts when triggers are hit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator prototype (spreadsheet + script) that accepts team-level skill coverage distributions and outputs probability of delivering top-3 initiatives at 60/80/95% confidence.
- One-pager tranche policy with numerical examples (5/10/15% reserve) and recommended hedging rules for cross-team blockers.
- Emergency trim playbook with checklist for PM/Eng/Design, sample Slack/Docs communications, and an example of a canary rollback for mission-critical work.
- Presentation to GTM and Eng leadership and incorporation of feedback into final playbook.

Deliverables:
- sources: a Google Sheet model and a CLI script for quick monte-carlo runs.
- Playbook doc: Confluence page - "Cycle Probabilistic Burn & Tranche Reserve Playbook".
- Trim templates: email/slack templates, retiming guidelines, and a decision-scorecard.

Approach:
1) Data gather (3 days): pull historical cycle-level burn curves, team-level velocity variance, and past emergency trims. 2) Model build (4 days): spreadsheet prototype, validate against 6 historical cycles. 3) Policy draft (2 days): generate tranche recommendations and gating logic. 4) Playbook + templates (2 days). 5) Review + iterate (ongoing).

Stakeholders: Marcus Li (assigned PM), Priya Natarajan (Head of Product Ops), Samir Patel (Eng manager), Lina Gomez (Design lead), Ops on-call.

Success metrics: Faster mid-cycle decisions (median trim decision time reduced from 3 days to <24 hours), improved accuracy of commit windows (predicted 80% confidence bands cover actual delivered work >75% of the time), and a measurable reduction in last-week scope slippage.
